sources.citation: Christopher R. Green, Academia.edu profile (the Internet Archive 2026-08-30) + ORCID 0000-0003-2766-2314 works + Crossref/DOAJ/HAL queries
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Green's Jarawan output = the two Mbat papers and the numerals paper; 'currently am working on a Jarawan documentation project funded by the NEH'. No Bankal/Gwak/Jar phonology exists in print.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Change Request 2011-172 (Rueck & Yoder, SIL Nigeria): split of jar into jjr and jgk
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic only (intelligibility, identity, 'no significant body of existing Jar literature').

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: new data and its relation to Bantu. Circulation draft ms, Cambridge, 12 Jan 2006, 20 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlists only; no prosody. Source review p. 2: 'An M.A. thesis on Jar provides a phonological sketch and wordlist of one Jarawan lect' (= Yabilsu 1991); Kraft 1981 has 'lengthy wordlists of Bankal.. in a rather doubtful transcription'.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jarawa = No. 253, Group G Central Bauci: vocabulary from Koelle 1854 and Mr Bieneman (p. 716 ff.), 'two dialects: Bununu and Zungur'. Introduction's notation note (accent ' 'so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable' that it is marked only for exceptions) is a Bantu-wide transcription convention, not a statement about Jarawa.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2026. The Jarawan Bantu languages in Nigeria; what is new research telling us? Jos Linguistic Circle slides (Academia.edu via the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jar-cluster tree (Zhar, Gwak, Zugur, Ndangshi, Doori, Mbat, Muun, Kantana, Damul); 'Christopher Green.. working remotely on Mbat, Galamkya, Kulung'; only Labir and Gura phonology given; nothing on Bankal/Gwak, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: OLAC resources for Gwak [jgk] (the Internet Archive 2026-01-22)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 2008 SIL Jar-survey audio wordlists (Yoder & Muniru, Gwak dialect, Garam village; PARADISEC RB5 Doori/Galamkya items), Glottolog, Ethnologue; no description.

sources.citation: ANR project ANR-25-CE54-1452, La structure, l'origine et l'evolution des langues jarawa (Van de Velde, LLACAN, from Dec 2025)
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: 'Malgre un siecle d'interet scientifique, les langues jarawa n'ont jamais ete documentees ou analysees'; focus Mbula; nothing on Jar stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Uebersee 97. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288 (open access)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Tone table p. 24: 'Jarawan -- No analysis'; p. 24: 'Some families, such as Jarawan, lack a single reliable synchronic description of tone.' ATR table p. 20 'Jarawan Absent Rueck et al. (2009)'; vowel table p. 22 'Jarawan Jar Rueck et al. (2009)'.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2020. Harmony and disharmony in Mbat (Jarawan Bantu) verbs. Linguistique et langues africaines 6: 43-72. doi:10.4000/lla.289
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Mbat = bada1258, not jara1263. pp. 50-51: three surface tone levels H/M/L plus a super-low, 'tonal system is still a work in progress'; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Entry 214 Jar cluster, p. 48.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue entry: Refs Maddieson & Williamson (1975); Shimizu (1983); Survey: Rueck et al 2009; Comparative: Shimizu (1983). No phonology.

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1988. A note on verbal extensions in Jarawan Bantu. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 3-8.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Verbal extensions in Jaar' pp. 5-6 and Table 2 rows Jaar/Bankal: perfect -Vm and future/habitual -Vn allomorphs chosen by stem weight (consonant count, vowel length). Table 3 (p. 6) heading '3. Heavy stress' is a misprint for 'Heavy stems' (page image checked). Data are tone-marked; no statement on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Group G, Jara/Jarawa (No. 253), pp. 179-180: 'exhibits a phonology which is alien to Bantu laws. Consonantal endings are common.. Consonants can apparently be pronounced doubly'; nothing on accent, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page jara1263 Jarawa (Nigeria) (+ dialect pages bank1257 Bankal, ging1241 Gingwak; ref 701778.bib)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all: refs are Green 2022 (subclassification), Maddieson & Williamson 1975, Ethnologue; both dialect nodes carry only Ethnologue 28 (2025). ISO split note: 'Intelligibility and lexical similarity between Bankal and Gwak are marginal.'

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. & Rebecca Grollemund. Jarawan languages: perspectives on (re)classification. Berlin: De Gruyter.

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J., Nengak Bako, Luther Hon, John Muniru, Linus Otronyi & Zachariah Yoder. 2009. Preliminary impressions from the sociolinguistic survey of the Jar dialects. ms. Jos (SIL Nigeria).

sources.note: Unpublished SIL survey of the Jar dialects (Bankal, Gwak, Duguri, Mbat, Galamkya); Blench 2024 cites it for Jar vowel inventory and ATR, so it carries some phonological notes on Bankal/Gwak proper.

sources.citation: Yabilsu, J. Kulu. 1991. The phonology of Jar: Galamkya dialect. M.A. thesis, University of Port Harcourt.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only phonological sketch of any Jar-cluster lect (Blench 2006 p. 2); Galamkya is a Mbat/Bada lect (bada1258) per Blench's Atlas, so it would be identity-noted, but it is the only place a word-prosody statement for the cluster is likely to have been.
